Bulletin SMB16-0008  Arrived. Checked in with management. Disabled fire alarm. Located RTU. Machine not running upon arrival. No call for cooling, heating, fan. Found two active alarms. T054, B1 failure. T613, economizer actuator overload, setpoint not reached. Machine is not under warranty. I reset alarms and powered machine off. Verified 0v. Installed supply fan ground wire per bulletin instructions. Ohm value is .2 ohms. Powered RTU on. Service test mode supply fan at several different speeds to prove operation. Machine needs a new scrolling marquee. No call for any action upon departure. Buttoned up panels. Cleaned up work area. Checked out with customer.

SUPPLEMENT TO WAF  BJWF04-232789 FOR:    Warranty rework per Hoskins . 7/17/17-Located RTU. Hauled tools, equipment to roof. Met Tom. Reconfigured condenser fans according to his request. Relocated BP and SP sensors with extended tubing, wiring to his request. Buttoned up RTU. Cleaned up work area.

Arrived on site, check in with Troy, get burn permit. Troy had a guy fire watching for me. Pressurized system found leak on north side of compressor discharge line repair cracked piping by brazing. Add nitrogen & leak checked with 80# nitrogen. Evacuate & charge system with 15.4# of refrigerant. Start A compressor & ran for 3-4 minutes & Freon started leaking on the south side of the fitting. Reclaimed what gas was left & repair south side of fitting- used trace gas & nitrogen to retest weld check ok. Ran vacuum pump to evacuate & left 7# holding charge till I can return. Called Troy with update.  Arrived on site, check in with Troy. Recheck leak area & pressurize to 650# Add 8# of 410A to complete charge. Run to test & checks ok. Complete paperwork for start up.

Check in with Troy- investigate and record configurations/set points - no alarms.  Document set points & configuration menu. Found alarm 170 stating a bad heat sensor thermistor. Need to order part.  No additional time was needed on 7/22 return visit.

Unit reported to have a bad #2 thermistor for the staged gas heat board.  Checked unit and found an alert for a failed #2 thermistor.  Checked connections for the thermistor wires and found them all very loose.  Remade all connections and alert cleared from the unit.
Gas valves not wired correctly from factory. GV2 harness connected to GV3 and GV3 harness connected to GV2. Corrected issue.

The EDT temperature wasn???t reading the correct temperature ( about 35 degrees to low). I tested the resistance on all 4 sensors. Approximately 12 K each.   I tested the wiring while I was tested the sensors and found a bad connection at one of the sensors. I repaired the connection ( bottom sensor in the middle). I checked the temperature and it was reading 70 degrees instead of 40 degrees. RAT,MAT, and EDT were reading almost the same.

There was not an active alert for this but it was in the alarm history. Checked wire connections at the staged gas heat board and found all connections very loose. Remade connections for all 3 thermistors associated with the staged gas heat board. This should resolve the intermittent issue with the unit.

called into service engineering for tech support case # 01211471. We found that the unit had extra wires for a smoke safety that didn???t need to be landed to the MBB board. I cut the extra wires and capped them off. I then verified that the unit is operational for the fire smoke shutdown. Job is completed.

Removed roof panels above the leaking section and dried them out inside the building. Put back together with silicon in the seams to prevent future leaks.

Removed filters, baffles, and panels. Check out the panel between the intake and exhaust hoods. Removed screws and flattened panel against the gasket until the factory rivets were against the panel. The rivers are holding the panel from sealing properly. Called roll about the problem and any bulletins. Didn???t get a final answer for a fix. Sent pictures for Roll. All of that model on the roof have the same problem. Reassembled unit.

Looking for roof leak. On bottom of unit that the unit sets over the roof curb. There???s a piece of channel that allows water from the condensation of the suction and compressor to run down and onto the roof. This channel on both ends was sealed with packing tape and allowing water to back up and allowing it to run under roof curb. Removed and watched ok. Also went to every unit and removed all tape from the ends.
Ran water over unit to reveal leak. Applied caulking to seal various areas of possible leaks. See attached CSR for full work details.

AT THE TIME OF STARTUP THE TECH NOTED ISSUES WITH THE WEATHER STRIPPING. NEEDS TO REPAIR OR REPLACE.  During start up of unit found filter door weather stripping not sealing properly. Applied new weather stripping for tighter seal. Found large air leak behind factory installed supply air smoke detector. Allowing excessive supply air to be drawn into heating combustion cabinet. Sealed off openings. Found condensate water entering secondary drain pan. Removed siding of unit to access evaporator section alongside primary drain pan. Found top evaporator drain pan hose was not draining into lower primary pan. Hose was strapped in correctly. Relocated fastener. Reinstalled siding and caulked FPT primary connection. All ok at this time.
